character_sheet: A small hostile rat: a 5x3x10 body with a spine ridge, a 3x2x4 head with a nose and two nub ears, two stub front legs, two haunches and a two-piece tail 21 long (RatModel.java:55-77, twelve parts), drawn at x0.75. 5 HP, 3 damage, 1 armour, speed 0.25 (EntityRat.java:77-84). On a 1-in-5 tick it picks the nearest living thing in a 9-block box - not the water creatures, other rats, the dungeon beast or a creative player (:157-165, :200-233) - runs at it at 1.25 with its attacking flag up and, within 2 blocks, bites on a double dice (:160-165); a rat with an owner (the summons of the Rat Sword, setOwner :114-118) spares the owner, their pets and, by config, all players (:212-222), follows the owner beyond 8 blocks at 1.75 and teleports to them beyond 16 (:168-181); wild rats despawn, owned rats stay (:100-104). It spawns in the dark, in the Crystal dimension only below y 50 with air around its head, at most eight together (:261-278; ModEntities.java:277-279). Read it as a rat: a scurry on four stubs, the tail whipping when it hunts.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.75 of the rig (RatRenderer.java:25, :38; shadow 0.075, :27) on a 64x64 sheet (RatModel.java:78), rat.png (RatRenderer.java:20); the hitbox is 0.25 x 0.5 (ModEntities.java:277-279). The original's ModelRat(1.0f) argument was the wingspeed (RatRenderer.java:15-16), not a scale. The tail's second piece is placed 9 px along the first each tick (RatModel.java:100-101) - key the joint, not the position.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1; the right front and left haunch one way, the left front and right haunch the other; 0 below the threshold
groups.plain: the four stubs scurry fore and aft in diagonal pairs with the stride
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.7 * 1.0) * pi * 0.25 * amount : 0; rfleg.xRot = lrleg.xRot = a; lfleg.xRot = rrleg.xRot = -a
groups.phase: the limbSwingAmount threshold of 0.1 gates it
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.7: the natural period is 2 pi / 1.7 = 3.70 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.axis: y (and the second piece's x / z position)
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.05 = 0.157 rad (9 deg) at 0.4 rad/tick - the first piece at 0.5x (4.5 deg), the second at 1.25x (11 deg); attacking: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) at 1.5 rad/tick (22 and 56 deg); the second piece is placed 9 px along the first's yaw
groups.plain: the tail sways side to side, the tip more than the root: a gentle sway at rest, a fast wide thrash while the attacking flag is up
groups.math: a = attacking ? cos(t * 1.5) * pi * 0.25 : cos(t * 0.4) * pi * 0.05; tail1.yRot = a * 0.5; tail2.yRot = a * 1.25; tail2.z = tail1.z + cos(tail1.yRot) * 9; tail2.x = tail1.x + sin(tail1.yRot) * 9
groups.phase: the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (EntityRat.java:47-48, set 1 whenever the 1-in-5 pass finds prey in its 9-block box :157-160, 0 when it finds none :167) selects the branch
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.4 calm (a 15.7-tick period) and x 1.5 attacking (4.19 ticks)

behaviour: One gait rhythm above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 (RatModel.java:86-90): the four stubs scurry 45 degrees x the walking speed in diagonal pairs at 1.7 rad/tick, a 3.7-tick period - a fast patter at the 0.25 speed (EntityRat.java:81).

One branch on the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (EntityRat.java:47-48), raised on the 1-in-5 pass whenever prey is found in the 9-block box - at any distance, through the whole chase (:157-160) - and dropped when the pass finds none (:167): the two-piece tail sways 4.5 and 11 degrees at 0.4 rad/tick at rest and thrashes 22 and 56 degrees at 1.5 rad/tick while the flag is up, the second piece placed 9 px along the first (RatModel.java:95-101).

The body, spine ridge, head, nose and ears are static; the head does not follow the look. The bite (doHurtTarget within 2 blocks when nextInt(8) == 0 or nextInt(7) == 1, EntityRat.java:162-165) and the owned rat's teleport to its owner (:174-179) draw no pose.
